zh.ONE_LINER_2_LINE_SUBTITLE: 它卖的不是笔记软件，是「你不用再花三个月，先把自己的系统搭出来」
zh.CATEGORY: 对象化个人知识管理（PKM）· 开箱即有结构
zh.USER_SCALE: 官方 why 页出示两行数字：50,000+ 活跃知识工作者、10,000+ Discord 社区成员；PH 4.8 分（官网 badge 写 198 条评价，PH 产品页实采 66 条，两个口径不一致）；App Store 4.28 / 116 个评分；G2 仅 1 条评论，样本不足
zh.BUSINESS_MODEL_SHORT: 软件白送，钱收在「调用」与「回顾」
zh.ASSUMPTIONS_ONE_PARAGRAPH_LIST_WHAT_IS_I: 三类输入：（1）可核实的公开材料——官网首页、why 页、定价页、whats-next（2026-09-08）、whats-not-next、六张官方对比页（obsidian / evernote / tana / heptabase / anytype / notion）、PH 66 条、G2 1 条、App Store 40 条；（2）一手实测——2026-11-11 由燃冰完成 20 分钟实测，文件名《2026-11-11 Capacities 真实体验》，注册引导、对象创建、AI 墙、首篇笔记用时都在里面；（3）我的判断——凡标 [推断] 或（我的判断）的都不是事实。
zh.VERDICT_ONE_LINER: Notion 卖自由度，Obsidian 卖所有权，Capacities 卖「不用搭」——代价是它替你决定结构长什么样。
zh.VERDICT_BODY_2_3_LINES: 可核实：官方把「不做团队、不做插件、不做端到端加密」写成了公开清单（whats-not-next），把「打谁」写进了 URL（/compare 六个竞品全部 200，/vs、/alternatives、/switch 全部 404）。实测（燃冰）：注册流程里就有使用引导，打开到写第一篇笔记 1 分钟，全程没有卡住。但它的 AI 全在 Pro 之后，免费版拿到的是「结构」，不是「智能」。
zh.TLDR_1_HEADLINE: 它把「配置成本」当成头号敌人
zh.TLDR_1_BODY: why 页第一句就是「Stop building your system. Start using it.」，整页在骂 Notion 的数据库搭建和 Obsidian 的插件维护
zh.TLDR_2_HEADLINE: 钱不赚在整理，赚在调用
zh.TLDR_2_BODY: 免费版给无限 object、无限自定义类型、全平台同步；AI、查询、任务、日历、语义检索全在 Pro 之后
zh.TLDR_3_HEADLINE: 它替 agent 做完了脏活
zh.TLDR_3_BODY: 实测（燃冰）的判断：它已经把人、书、会议、项目清洗成带字段的对象，这正好是 personal agent 最缺的输入层
zh.TTV_NOTE_WHAT_HAPPENS_AT_AHA: 实测（燃冰）：从打开官网到写出一篇像样的笔记 1 分钟，因为使用说明直接嵌在注册流程里，不是看完文档再回来
zh.LOOP_FREQ_NOTE_TRIGGER_CONTEXT: 每日笔记是日频入口；对象关系网是被动生长的，不需要每天维护
zh.MOAT_REASONING_ONE_LINE: 对象模型 7、开箱结构 7、AI 4、生态 2、可迁移性 4，加权 6（我的评分，非测量）。它守住的不是技术，是「别人的系统你不想要」这件事
zh.SNAPSHOT_ONE_TO_TWO_SENTENCE_DEFINITION: 官网原话是「The studio for your mind」——a place for all your information。落到产品上：你的笔记不是文件，是有类型、有属性、有位置的 object，上传的 PDF 会自动落到 PDF 那一堆里，加一场会议它已经知道有日期和参与者。
zh.USER_PROMISE: 官网 why 页的承诺是三句：结构天生就有、每天一页当收件箱、每条链接都双向。翻成人话是「今天就能用，不用先设计系统」。
zh.CATEGORY_POSITIONING_PARAGRAPH: 一个反常识的定位事实：官网首页、定价页、whats-next 都没有把它归到 AI 工具类目里，whats-next 甚至写「AI in Capacities should stay assistive」。但它的付费墙恰恰卡在 AI 上——免费版没有 AI 助手，Pro 才有。所以它的真实位置是：用「不用搭」抢 Notion/Obsidian 的存量用户，用「AI 额度」做二次变现。
zh.ASSUMPTION_1: App Store 评分取自 iTunes lookup 接口（2026-11-11 核实：4.2845 / 116 个评分 / 版本 1.72.13）；40 条评论取自 iTunes 评论 RSS，不是官方榜单
zh.ASSUMPTION_2: 一手实测由燃冰于 2026-11-11 完成。其中「脏材料边界」（喂 8000 字长文看它会不会通顺地错）这一项当次没做，报告里不给结论
zh.SHOT_1_CAPTION: 官网首图：它把知识管理拍成了画廊，不是在展示功能表
zh.SHOT_2_CAPTION: 一本书的 object 页：作者、状态、评分都是字段——它的护城河候选就在这张图里
zh.SHOT_3_CAPTION: 每日笔记 + 图谱：今天写的东西自己挂到关系网里，这是它的核心循环
zh.SHOT_4_CAPTION: 「今天就是收件箱」：碎片先进每日笔记，以后再升级成 object
zh.SHOT_5_CAPTION: 反向链接与未链接提及：它主张「按你怎么想去找，而不是按你怎么归档去找」
zh.SHOT_6_CAPTION: 官方自述团队 7 人、完全独立自营（whats-next 2026-09-08 原文）
zh.SEGMENT_1_NAME: 换过三四个笔记软件、还没找到系统的知识工作者
zh.SEGMENT_1_DETAIL: PH 评论里的迁移链很清楚：Evernote → Notion → Roam → Obsidian → Capacities。这批人不是没工具，是被「搭系统」耗光了耐心。实测（燃冰）：对象就是书、项目、人、每日笔记、灵感五类，一打开就知道干嘛。
zh.SEGMENT_2_NAME: 研究者、写作者、终身学习者（个人为主）
zh.SEGMENT_2_DETAIL: 官方对比页把 Best For 写成 researchers / writers / lifelong learners，落在功能上是阅读笔记、会议、项目、人脉这几条线。实测（燃冰）：输入书名《深度工作》，它自动补齐作者等结构化信息，不用手打。
zh.SEGMENT_3_NAME: 想给 AI 喂干净上下文的个人用户
zh.SEGMENT_3_DETAIL: Pro 里有 AI Chat Connectors（ChatGPT / Claude / Cursor 可直接建改 object）和 REST API 2.0。实测（燃冰）的原话判断是：它的字段设计本身可以当 personal agent 的结构化样本学。注意这批人是「用得起 Pro」的人，免费版拿不到 AI。
zh.TRIGGER_MOMENT: 两个时刻：一是又一次把笔记从 A 搬到 B 之后；二是开始用 AI，发现自己的笔记库根本没法喂给模型
zh.FREQUENCY: 记录与回顾是每天（每日笔记）；对象关系网是被动积累，不需要日常维护
zh.USAGE_CONTEXT: 读书笔记、会议纪要、项目推进、人脉维护、灵感碎片、给 AI 当上下文库
zh.JTBD_FUNCTIONAL: 把读过、见过、聊过的东西存成有类型的东西，需要时能找到
zh.JTBD_EMOTIONAL: 「我不想再当自己笔记系统的项目经理」——配置和维护本身是一种隐形劳动
zh.JTBD_SOCIAL: 看上去是个有体系的人（而不是装了一屏 App 的人）
zh.LOOP_TRIGGER_DETAIL: 今天要读一本书 / 要开一个会 / 想到一个点子
zh.LOOP_ACTION_DETAIL: 在每日笔记里写下碎片，或者直接建一个 object（书 / 会议 / 人），填几个字段
zh.LOOP_REWARD_DETAIL: 打开那个人或那本书，今天写的东西已经在它下面；反向链接自己长出来了
zh.LOOP_RETURN_DETAIL: 第二天的每日笔记空了，但关系网更厚了；攒得越久，越舍不得换（也越难换）
zh.LOOP_ONE_LINE_INSIGHT_WHAT_THE_LOOP_ACTU: 这个循环教用户的是：结构不是设计出来的，是写出来的。所以它真正的产品不是编辑器，是那套「先有类型、后有内容」的默认值。
zh.ACQUISITION_LOOP_DETAIL: 官方未披露渠道结构。可核实的三条：① 六张对比页吃长尾搜索（capacities vs obsidian / evernote / notion 这类意图离付费最近）；② 官网直接对着 Notion 与 Obsidian 的用户喊话，why 页整页是「你搭了一堆没用的数据库」的共鸣稿；③ PH 三次发布 + 4.8 分长期挂着。
zh.AHA_MOMENT_DETAIL: 官方押的 aha 是「上传 PDF 它自己落到 PDF 那堆」；实测（燃冰）真实触发的 aha 是另一件事——输入书名，字段自己填好了，第一次不用手打结构化信息
zh.RETENTION_1: 对象关系网随时间变厚：写得越久，打开一个人就能看到全部上下文，换工具等于放弃这张网
zh.RETENTION_2: 每日笔记养成的日频习惯，是它最稳的一条留存（评论里高频出现「brain dump 完以后再整理」）
zh.RETENTION_3: 导出与导入都在免费档（定价页原文：Import and export to Markdown, CSV, and more — 三个档位都含），所以锁定不靠数据，靠习惯与关系网
zh.VIRALITY_DETAIL_OR_NONE: 弱传播，但有明确形态：查看权限（view-only sharing）在免费档，天然是分享入口；真正被传播的是截图式的「我的 object 页长这样」。它不做邀请返利。
zh.SURFACE_1_ROLE: 默认首页兼收件箱：今天的所有输入先落这里，和日历并排
zh.SURFACE_2_NAME: Object 页（书 / 人 / 会议 / 项目）
zh.SURFACE_2_ROLE: 产品的真正主场：属性 + 正文 + 反向链接 + 相关对象，一个东西只存一次
zh.SURFACE_3_ROLE: 个人 / 工作分仓，免费版就不限数量
zh.SURFACE_4_ROLE: Pro 功能：按类型、标签、语义把对象重新组织成视图——回顾层
zh.SURFACE_5_ROLE: 把关系网画出来；对个人是情绪价值，对 AI 是检索入口
zh.SURFACE_6_NAME: AI 面板与 Explore 对话
zh.SURFACE_6_ROLE: Pro 功能：划词翻译/摘要、属性自动填充、图片 OCR、跨库问答
zh.ENTITY_2: Object Type（自定义类型 + 属性）
zh.IA_LOGIC_PARAGRAPH: 没有文件夹，也没有数据库要你设计。第一层是「这是什么类型」，第二层是「它有哪些属性」，第三层是「它连到谁」。这三层是预置的，用户只是在往里填——这就是它和 Notion（要你设计库）、Obsidian（要你设计文件夹）最根本的差别。
zh.NAV_INTERACTION_PARAGRAPH: 主路径只有两个：@ 引用一个对象、/ 插入一个块。学会这两个，产品就通了；学不会也不会卡死，因为注册流程里有引导。实测（燃冰）：全程没有「下一步该点哪」的时刻。
zh.CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: 它所有的手艺都指向一件事：把「先配置、后使用」的顺序倒过来——先给你能用的结构，配置变成使用过程中的副产品。
zh.CRAFT_1_NAME: 对象类型 + 属性继承
zh.CRAFT_1_DETAIL: 定义一次类型，同类型的所有对象共享属性；给类型加一个字段，已有对象全部获得。这是它对抗 Notion「每个库都要单独设计」的核心手法
zh.CRAFT_2_DETAIL: 不用插件、不用写查询，提到谁，谁下面就有一条。对比页原话：Backlinks by default，No query to write
zh.CRAFT_3_DETAIL: 把「先决定放哪」这个动作从入口拿掉：今天写的东西先落当天那一页，以后再升级成 object。WhatsApp / Telegram / 邮件都能往里投
zh.CRAFT_4_NAME: 预置示例与流程内引导
zh.CRAFT_4_DETAIL: 每个类型自带默认案例，用官方文档教你怎么用。实测（燃冰）：使用说明嵌在注册流程里，所以打开到写出第一篇只有 1 分钟
zh.CRAFT_5_DETAIL: 白板、查询、日历、任务、AI 全是官方内建（whats-not-next 明确写不做插件）。代价是长尾需求没人接，收益是一致性和速度
zh.TTV_LABEL: 价值到达时间：1 分钟（实测）
zh.COG_LABEL: 认知负荷：低（实测：全程没卡）
zh.DELIGHT_LABEL: 惊喜感：中高（实测：书名自动补字段）
zh.TRUST_LABEL: 信任机制：不用 AI 就不共享数据（文档原文）
zh.STRUGGLE_LABEL: 上手难度：低；难的是迁移
zh.DELIGHT_1: 实测（燃冰）：输入书名《深度工作》，它自己把结构化信息填好了，不用手打——这是产品最像「智能」的一刻，而且发生在免费流程里
zh.DELIGHT_2: 实测（燃冰）：注册流程本身就是引导，不需要看文档、不需要找教程
zh.DELIGHT_3: 免费档给无限 object、无限自定义类型、全平台同步、导入导出、只读分享（定价页三档对比可核实）——它把「整理」彻底白送
zh.STRUGGLE_1: 实测（燃冰）：把已有内容搬进来会遇到类型不匹配——它的对象类型是它定义的，你的旧笔记没有这些字段
zh.STRUGGLE_2: 免费版摸不到 AI：定价表里 Basic 那一行 AI 是 Not included。奔着「AI 笔记」来的人会在第一次想用 AI 时撞墙
zh.STRUGGLE_3: 实测（燃冰）原话判断：想自己定制一些东西，它不合适。自由度被换掉了，这是设计选择不是缺陷
zh.REVENUE_MODEL_NAME: 免费核心 + Pro 订阅 + AI 加购（Plus）
zh.REVENUE_MODEL_DETAIL: 定价页（港区，2026-11 采集）：Basic 免费永久；Pro HK$77.99/月、Believer HK$98.99/月（月付价），年付 -16%；Plus 加购 HK$66.67/月（年付），给更大的 AI 额度，用超了可再买 top-up。官方对比页统一用美元口径：Pro $9.99/月（按年付）。Believer 的差别是「支持团队 + 新功能内测」，不是功能更多。
zh.FREE_PAID_DETAIL: 免费给的是「结构 + 存储」：无限 object / 空间 / 自定义类型、全平台同步、离线、导入导出、只读分享、从 WhatsApp / Telegram / 邮件捕获。Pro 才给「调用 + 回顾」：AI 助手、智能查询、任务、日历集成、语义检索、版本历史、未链接提及、白板、Readwise / Kindle 导入、公开 API、图片与 PDF 分析。（依据：定价页三档对比表）
zh.MON_ENTRY_HEADLINE: 把整理白送，把调用收钱
zh.MON_ENTRY_DETAIL: 它没有像同类那样按存储或对象数量限免费档，反而把最容易被骂的容量做成无限。收钱的两层都很「用起来之后才有感觉」：AI（想让它替我读）和查询/日历/任务（想让它替我安排）。这个切法的好处是免费用户永远用得下去，坏处是「AI 笔记」这个招牌与免费体验有落差。
zh.UX_MON_HEADLINE: 基本对齐，有一处结构性张力
zh.UX_MON_DETAIL_ARE_THEY_ALIGNED_OR_IN_TEN: 对齐的部分：免费档不阉割核心承诺（结构、同步、导出都在），用户越用关系网越厚，越有理由升级。张力有两处：① AI 是它最响的卖点，却完全在付费墙后，第一次想用必然撞墙；② 官方明说不做端到端加密，而用 AI 就会把数据共享给模型供应商（文档原文）——愿意付费的个人用户，必须同时接受这两件事。
zh.COMP_INTRO: 以下对比是我的主观判断，不是评分或测量。AI 内置度这一列按「官方是否内置」评，不按社区插件评。
zh.COMP_1_D1: 极高（本地 md 文件）
zh.COMP_WHERE_OWN_WINS: 开箱结构与上手曲线。这是它唯一敢在 slogan 上写的东西：Stop building your system。实测（燃冰）印证了——注册流程里就有引导，1 分钟写出第一篇，全程没有「下一步点哪」的时刻。
zh.COMP_WHERE_RIVALS_CATCH: 数据所有权与自由度。Anytype 与 Obsidian 把「文件归你」做成了默认值；Obsidian 的生态规模是它结构上放弃的东西（Capacities 自己的对比页写 Obsidian 有 2,700+ 社区插件，而 Obsidian 社区站 2026-11 的计数是 10,194 个——对比页的数字会过期，这本身就是个提示）。团队协作则被 Notion 全拿走，且官方明确不打算抢。
zh.CHANNEL_1: 六张官方对比页吃长尾搜索（/compare/obsidian、evernote、notion、tana、heptabase、anytype 全部 200）
zh.CHANNEL_2: Reddit 与 Discord 口碑（官网自述 10,000+ 社区成员），why 页直接引用 r/capacitiesapp 的用户原话
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_1_DETAIL: 对比页 + 官方迁移指南（docs 里有 Obsidian import guide / switching guide）。它专门接「从别处搬过来」的人，这条链路离付费最近，因为搬家的人已经付过一次学费。
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_2_DETAIL: Discord 1 万人、Reddit 分版，传播物是「我的 object 页长这样」。它没有插件市场，所以生态的载体是模板和截图，而不是代码。
zh.HORIZONTAL_1: 全平台客户端：Web、Mac、Windows、Linux、iOS、Android（定价页数据档一行写全）
zh.HORIZONTAL_2: AI Chat Connectors：让 ChatGPT / Claude / Cursor 直接读写你的 object（定价页 Pro 行）
zh.VERTICAL_1: 个人知识管理：研究者、写作者、终身学习者（官方对比页 Best For 原话）
zh.VERTICAL_2: 团队与协作：官方明确不做（whats-not-next：Collaboration & Team plans — on hold）
zh.PLATFORM_1: 公开 REST API 2.0 + TypeScript SDK（Pro 档），第三方可以读写成对象
zh.PLATFORM_2: 没有插件市场：whats-not-next 明写 Plugins 不在计划内，扩展性只能走 API
zh.CURRENT_AI_USAGE_PARAGRAPH: AI 全部锁在 Pro 及以上。能力面（官方文档）：Explore 里的 AI Chat、划词 AI 面板（翻译/重写/摘要）、自动打标签、自动归集、属性自动填充、图片分析（含 OCR 与手写）、/Ask AI、AI 生成查询。官方立场写得很克制：whats-next 说 AI 应该 stay assistive，grounded in your notes，never in the way of your own thinking。实测（燃冰）：免费版确实摸不到 AI，墙只在 AI 与任务/探索模块触发；不用 AI 时数据不会共享给模型供应商（文档原文），实测时也看到了这条强隐私提示。
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_1: 未上线（我的判断）：把属性自动填充升级成「读完脏材料后提议一套 object 结构，等你确认」——现在它是填已有字段，不是提议结构
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_2: 未上线（我的判断）：让 Connectors 从「建改单个 object」升级成「批量重构整个空间」（API 2.0 已具备读的基础）
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_3: 未上线（我的判断）：结构体检——告诉用户哪些对象缺关键字段，导致 AI 读不懂。这是它唯一能不做模型、只做结构的位置
zh.AI_OPPORTUNITY_1: （我的判断）它最该做的不是更强的 AI，而是把「字段设计」变成可复用资产：书、会议、客户、项目的标准属性集。实测（燃冰）的判断就是「这套结构值得学，可以喂给自己的 AI」——说明用户已经把它当 schema 供应商，只差官方把这件事产品化
zh.AI_OPPORTUNITY_2: （我的判断）把 API 2.0 + Connectors 做成 agent 的记忆后端：agent 写日志、写结论、写待办都进对象层，人负责确认。这是它从「笔记软件」变成「基础设施」的唯一路径
zh.AI_DISRUPTION_RISK: （我的判断）真正的威胁不是竞品做 AI，而是通用 agent 自己长出对象模型。当 ChatGPT / Claude 能维护你的个人知识图谱，用户就不再为「对象页长什么样」付第二份订阅——它现在替 agent 做的那层清洗工作，正是 agent 迟早自己会做的
zh.METRICS_INTRO: 官方不披露活跃、付费转化与流失，下面三张卡是可核实数字 + 明确标注的推断，不用假精度。
zh.NORTH_STAR_METRIC: 周活跃 space 数 [推断]
zh.NORTH_STAR_WHY: 推断依据：它的价值只在「每天打开写一点」时发生（每日笔记是唯一日频入口）；官网只露出 5 万活跃知识工作者这个大数，没有日活/周活口径
zh.INPUT_METRIC_1_WHY: 推断依据：官方说自己是 fully independent、团队 7 人（whats-next 原文），收入结构里 Pro 是主梁；按 $9.99/月 反推，团队规模与订阅量互相约束
zh.INPUT_METRIC_2_NAME: AI 额度消耗与 Plus 加购率 [推断]
zh.INPUT_METRIC_2_WHY: 推断依据：Plus 加购（HK$66.67/月，年付）是它唯一的二次变现杠杆，定价页专门写了 top-up 与 auto top-up，说明这项已经被当成收入线在设计
zh.INPUT_METRIC_3_WHY: 推断依据：每日笔记是核心循环的入口，也是它和 Obsidian/Notion 最不一样的地方；这个数的趋势比 object 总数更能说明产品有没有被用起来
zh.GUARDRAIL_METRIC: 移动端崩溃与同步失败率 [推断]
zh.GUARDRAIL_WHY: 推断依据：App Store 实采 40 条里 1-3 星占多数，落点全在分享面板坏数月、同步要重启、iPad 布局，「Desktop is Lifechanging, iOS is Barely Functional」是标题级原话——这条体验崩了，桌面端做得再好也会被差评拖住
zh.METRIC_BLINDSPOT_WHY: 实测（燃冰）判断：最大短板是用户把旧内容搬进来时类型对不上。这类失败在后台大概率只被记成「导入成功」，因为对象确实建出来了，只是字段是空的
zh.FRICTION_1_BODY_WHY_IT_MATTERS: 实测（燃冰）：它的对象类型是它定义的，你的旧笔记没有这些字段，所以「搬进来」不等于「用起来」。这是它「开箱即用」承诺的反面：对新用户开箱，对老用户不通用。
zh.FRICTION_2_TITLE: 移动端不是同一个产品
zh.FRICTION_2_BODY: App Store 3★ 标题原话「Desktop is Lifechanging, iOS is Barely Functional」；同批评论里还有「share from an app via sharesheet 已经坏了几个月」「同步要重启 App」「iPad 上不能建 object」。而 capture 恰恰是移动端唯一的用途。
zh.FRICTION_3_BODY: 实测（燃冰）原话：如果用户想定制一些东西，它不合适。没有插件、没有高级自动化与公式（whats-not-next 明列），所以重度用户的天花板很低——它不是给 tinkerer 的。
zh.FRICTION_4_TITLE: 免费版零 AI，与招牌不符
zh.FRICTION_4_BODY: 定价表可核实：Basic 档 AI 一行是 Not included。外部讨论里它常被当成「AI 笔记」，第一次想用 AI 就是付费墙。这不是设计缺陷，但它是预期管理问题——文案卖的是 studio，用户听到的是 AI。
zh.RISK_INTRO: 只列有公开依据的风险；概率与严重度是我的判断，不做量化。
zh.RISK_1_NAME: 移动端体验断层拖住口碑
zh.RISK_1_LIK: App Store 40 条中 1-3 星占多数，落点集中在分享面板、同步、iPad 布局
zh.RISK_1_MIT: 把移动端当 capture 专用件做，只保「3 秒记下」一条硬指标（我的建议）
zh.RISK_2_NAME: 隐私叙事有结构性缺口
zh.RISK_2_LIK: whats-not-next 明写不做端到端加密；用 AI 时部分数据共享给模型供应商（官方文档原文）
zh.RISK_2_MIT: 把「不用 AI 就不共享」做成可见开关与年检报告，用透明换信任（我的建议）
zh.RISK_3_NAME: 通用 agent 自己长出对象层
zh.RISK_3_LIK: ChatGPT / Claude / Cursor 已可通过 Connectors 直接建改它的对象（定价页原文），通道反向也成立
zh.RISK_3_MIT: 抢做 schema 与写入协议的事实标准，从「界面」退到「底座」（我的建议）
zh.RISK_4_NAME: 单一订阅价 + 7 人团队的天花板
zh.RISK_4_LIK: 自述团队 7 人、完全独立自营；Pro 单一价格档，5 万活跃 × $9.99 的规模上限可见
zh.RISK_4_MIT: 把 Plus 加购做成真正的第二收入线，或对 API/团队外的企业场景开放（我的建议）
zh.OPP_1_DETAIL_WHAT_HOW_WHY: （我的判断）它的公开短板就是「搬进来之后类型对不上」。做一次性迁移 + 类型映射（把 Notion/Obsidian 的旧结构映射到它的对象类型），成本极低、需求确定，而且这些人已经证明愿意付学费。
zh.OPP_2_HEADLINE: 把字段设计做成可复用资产
zh.OPP_2_DETAIL: （我的判断）它的对象类型是一套现成的 schema：书、人、会议、项目。实测（燃冰）的直接反应是「这套结构值得学，我要让我的 AI 用它」。官方把它当默认值，对外却是零文档化的资产——做成模板包、行业版本（投研/咨询/医生），是它不必写代码就能开的新收入口。
zh.OPP_3_DETAIL: （我的判断）用户不知道自己哪些对象 AI 读不懂。做一个「缺字段 / 缺链接 / 缺上下文」的检查清单，把它从「好看的笔记」推向「可被 agent 使用的知识库」。这件事不依赖模型能力，只依赖它已有的对象模型。
zh.STRATEGIC_HEADLINE: 从「笔记软件」变成「agent 的结构化记忆层」
zh.STRATEGIC_DETAIL_HIGH_IMPACT_BET: （我的判断）它真正的差异化不是 AI，是它已经替 agent 做完的那层清洗：人、书、会议、项目都被抽成了带字段的对象。押注应该是把这个结构变成 agent 可读写的默认 schema（API 2.0 + Connectors 已经在路上），而不是追着模型能力做功能。
zh.MOONSHOT_HEADLINE: 让它的对象规范成为个人 AI 的默认结构
zh.MOONSHOT_DETAIL_WHY_IT_COULD_RESHAPE_THE: （我的判断）如果 agent 记账、记人、记项目都按它的字段来写，那 Capacities 就从「一个 App」变成「个人 AI 的 schema 层」——类比不是 Notion，是数据库的连接器。它的 7 人团队做不了模型，但做得了标准；一旦标准被采用，迁移方向就反过来了。
zh.FINAL_WINS: 开箱结构与对象模型：不用搭、一打开就有类型，实测 1 分钟出第一篇
zh.FINAL_BREAKS: 移动端（capture 断裂）与迁移（类型对不上）；外加「想定制就不合适」这道天花板
zh.FINAL_MOAT_OR_LACK_THEREOF: 它的护城河是「别人的系统你不想要」这件事，不是技术。对象模型好抄，让用户相信「这次不用再搭了」不好抄——但这也意味着它挡不住通用 agent 从上游吃掉对象层。

en.ONE_LINER_2_LINE_SUBTITLE: It does not sell note-taking. It sells: you don't have to spend three months building the system first.
en.CATEGORY: Object-based personal knowledge management · structure out of the box
en.USER_SCALE: The official why page shows two numbers: 50,000+ active knowledge workers and 10,000+ Discord community members. Product Hunt 4.8 (the site badge claims 198 reviews; the product page itself carries 66 collected reviews — the two counts disagree). App Store 4.28 / 116 ratings. G2 has exactly 1 review, too small a sample to use.
en.BUSINESS_MODEL_SHORT: Software given away, money charged on retrieval and review
en.STAGE_MATURITY: Growth stage (three Product Hunt launches: 30 May 2023, 12 Jul 2023, 25 Jul 2024 for mobile; App Store build 1.72.13 updated 9 Nov 2026)
en.ASSUMPTIONS_ONE_PARAGRAPH_LIST_WHAT_IS_I: Three inputs. (1) Verifiable public material: homepage, why page, pricing page, whats-next (8 Sep 2026), whats-not-next, six official comparison pages (obsidian / evernote / tana / heptabase / anytype / notion), 66 Product Hunt reviews, 1 G2 review, 40 App Store reviews. (2) First-hand testing: a 20-minute hands-on session on 11 Nov 2026, written up as 2026-11-11 Capacities 真实体验 — onboarding, object creation, the AI paywall and time-to-first-note all come from there. (3) My judgement, always marked [inferred] or (my read).
en.VERDICT_ONE_LINER: Notion sells freedom, Obsidian sells ownership, Capacities sells not having to build anything — and the price is that it decides what your structure looks like.
en.VERDICT_BODY_2_3_LINES: Verifiable: the company publishes a list of things it will not build (no team plans, no plugins, no end-to-end encryption) and puts its competitive targets in the URL (/compare six rivals all return 200; /vs, /alternatives and /switch all return 404). Hands-on: onboarding guidance is built into the signup flow, first note in one minute, nothing blocked the way. But every AI feature sits behind Pro — the free tier gives you structure, not intelligence.
en.TLDR_1_HEADLINE: It treats configuration cost as the enemy
en.TLDR_1_BODY: The why page opens with “Stop building your system. Start using it.” and spends the rest of the page attacking Notion database-building and Obsidian plugin maintenance
en.TLDR_2_HEADLINE: It charges for retrieval, not for tidying
en.TLDR_2_BODY: Free gets unlimited objects, unlimited custom types and sync everywhere; AI, queries, tasks, calendar and semantic search all sit behind Pro
en.TLDR_3_HEADLINE: It already did the agent's dirty work
en.TLDR_3_BODY: Hands-on read: people, books, meetings and projects are already cleaned into typed objects with fields — exactly the input layer a personal agent is missing
en.TTV_NOTE_WHAT_HAPPENS_AT_AHA: Hands-on: one minute from opening the site to a proper first note, because the instructions are embedded in the signup flow rather than in a docs page you have to find
en.LOOP_FREQ_NOTE_TRIGGER_CONTEXT: The daily note is the daily entry point; the object graph grows passively and needs no daily upkeep
en.MOAT_REASONING_ONE_LINE: Object model 7, out-of-the-box structure 7, AI 4, ecosystem 2, portability 4 — weighted 6 (my rating, not a measurement). What it defends is not technology but the feeling that nobody wants someone else's system
en.SNAPSHOT_ONE_TO_TWO_SENTENCE_DEFINITION: The site calls it “The studio for your mind — a place for all your information”. In the product that means notes are not files: they are objects with a type, properties and a place. Upload a PDF and it lands with the other PDFs; add a meeting and it already knows about dates and attendees.
en.USER_PROMISE: The why page promises three things: structure is built in, every day gets a page as your inbox, and every link is bidirectional. In plain words: usable today, no system design required.
en.CATEGORY_POSITIONING_PARAGRAPH: One counter-intuitive fact: neither the homepage, the pricing page nor whats-next files it under AI tools — whats-next actually says “AI in Capacities should stay assistive”. Yet the paywall sits precisely on AI: free has no AI assistant, Pro does. So its real position is: take Notion and Obsidian's installed base by removing setup cost, then monetise a second time through AI credits.
en.ASSUMPTION_1: App Store figures come from the iTunes lookup endpoint (verified 11 Nov 2026: 4.2845 average, 116 ratings, version 1.72.13); the 40 reviews come from the iTunes review RSS feed, not an official chart
en.ASSUMPTION_2: The hands-on session was run on 11 Nov 2026. The dirty-material boundary (feeding it an 8,000-character document to see whether it fails fluently) was not tested, so this report draws no conclusion about it
en.SHOT_1_CAPTION: The hero image: knowledge management shot as a gallery, not a feature table
en.SHOT_2_CAPTION: A book object: author, status and rating are fields — the moat candidate is in this screenshot
en.SHOT_3_CAPTION: Daily note plus graph: what you write today attaches itself to the network — that is the core loop
en.SHOT_4_CAPTION: Today is the inbox: fragments land in the daily note and get promoted to objects later
en.SHOT_5_CAPTION: Backlinks and unlinked mentions — the pitch is structuring by how you think, not how you file
en.SHOT_6_CAPTION: The team describes itself as seven people, fully independent (whats-next, 8 Sep 2026)
en.SEGMENT_1_NAME: Knowledge workers on their third or fourth note app
en.SEGMENT_1_DETAIL: The migration chain in the reviews is explicit: Evernote → Notion → Roam → Obsidian → Capacities. These users are not short of tools; they ran out of patience for building systems. Hands-on: five obvious surfaces — books, projects, people, daily notes, ideas — and you know what to do immediately.
en.SEGMENT_2_NAME: Researchers, writers and lifelong learners (mostly solo)
en.SEGMENT_2_DETAIL: The comparison pages list Best For: researchers / writers / lifelong learners, which in the product means reading notes, meetings, projects and contacts. Hands-on: typing the book title Deep Work auto-filled the structured metadata — no manual entry.
en.SEGMENT_3_NAME: Solo users who want clean context to feed an AI
en.SEGMENT_3_DETAIL: Pro includes AI Chat Connectors (ChatGPT / Claude / Cursor can create and edit objects directly) and a REST API 2.0. The hands-on conclusion was that the field design itself is worth copying as a structured sample for a personal agent. Note that this segment has to be able to pay: free gets no AI.
en.TRIGGER_MOMENT: Two moments: after migrating notes from one app to another yet again; or on starting to use AI and realising the notes vault cannot be fed to a model at all
en.FREQUENCY: Capture and review are daily (the daily note); the object graph accumulates passively
en.USAGE_CONTEXT: Reading notes, meeting notes, project tracking, contact management, idea fragments, a context library for an AI
en.JTBD_FUNCTIONAL: Turn everything read, seen and discussed into typed things that can be found later
en.JTBD_EMOTIONAL: Stop being the project manager of your own note system — configuration and upkeep are invisible labour
en.JTBD_SOCIAL: Look like someone with a system, not someone with a screen full of apps
en.LOOP_TRIGGER_DETAIL: A book to read today, a meeting to attend, an idea that arrives
en.LOOP_ACTION_DETAIL: Drop the fragment into today's note, or create an object (book / meeting / person) and fill a few fields
en.LOOP_REWARD_DETAIL: Open that person or that book and today's writing is already under it; backlinks have grown by themselves
en.LOOP_RETURN_DETAIL: Tomorrow's daily note is empty, but the network is thicker — and the longer it accumulates, the less you want to leave (and the harder it becomes)
en.LOOP_ONE_LINE_INSIGHT_WHAT_THE_LOOP_ACTU: What the loop teaches is that structure is written, not designed. The real product is therefore not the editor but the default values: type first, content second.
en.ACQUISITION_LOOP_DETAIL: Channel mix is not disclosed. Three verifiable channels: (1) six comparison pages harvesting long-tail search intent such as capacities vs obsidian / evernote / notion, which sit closest to purchase; (2) the why page speaking directly to Notion and Obsidian users about wasted database-building; (3) three Product Hunt launches holding a 4.8 rating.
en.AHA_MOMENT_DETAIL: The company bets on the aha of a PDF filing itself with the other PDFs. The aha that actually fired in testing was different: type a book title and the fields fill themselves — the first time no manual structured data was needed.
en.RETENTION_1: The object graph thickens over time: open one person and every related context is there, so switching tools means abandoning the network
en.RETENTION_2: The daily-note habit is its steadiest retention driver (reviews repeatedly describe brain-dumping first and organising later)
en.RETENTION_3: Import and export to Markdown and CSV are included on all three tiers (pricing page), so lock-in is habit and graph, not data captivity
en.VIRALITY_DETAIL_OR_NONE: Weak but shaped: view-only sharing is on the free tier, so sharing is a natural outlet; what actually travels is screenshots of someone's object page. There is no referral programme.
en.SURFACE_1_ROLE: Default home and inbox: today's input lands here, next to the calendar
en.SURFACE_2_ROLE: The real home of the product: properties, body, backlinks, related objects — one thing stored once
en.SURFACE_3_ROLE: Personal and work separation; unlimited even on the free tier
en.SURFACE_4_ROLE: Pro feature: reorganise objects by type, tag or semantics — the review layer
en.SURFACE_5_ROLE: Draws the network; emotional value for humans, a retrieval surface for AI
en.SURFACE_6_ROLE: Pro features: translate/summarise a selection, auto-fill properties, image OCR, cross-library chat
en.IA_LOGIC_PARAGRAPH: There are no folders and no database for you to design. Layer one is what kind of thing this is; layer two is which properties it has; layer three is what it links to. All three are pre-built and the user only fills them in — the fundamental difference from Notion (design your own database) and Obsidian (design your own folders).
en.NAV_INTERACTION_PARAGRAPH: Two gestures cover the main path: @ to reference an object, / to insert a block. Learn those and the product is open; fail to learn them and you are still not stuck, because onboarding sits inside signup. Hands-on: there was never a moment of wondering where to click next.
en.CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: Every craft decision points at one thing: reverse the order of configure-then-use. You get a working structure first, and configuration becomes a by-product of using it.
en.CRAFT_1_DETAIL: Define a type once and every object of that type shares its properties; add a field to the type and existing objects get it too. This is the core move against Notion, where every database needs its own design
en.CRAFT_2_DETAIL: No plugin, no query to write: mention something and a link appears under it. The comparison page puts it plainly — Backlinks by default, no query to write
en.CRAFT_3_DETAIL: It removes the where-should-this-go decision from the entry point: today's writing lands on today's page and is promoted to an object later. WhatsApp, Telegram and email can all feed it
en.CRAFT_4_DETAIL: Every type ships with default examples and the docs teach inside the product. Hands-on: instructions were embedded in the signup flow, which is why the first note took one minute
en.CRAFT_5_DETAIL: Whiteboards, queries, calendar, tasks and AI are all first-party (whats-not-next states plugins are not planned). The cost is that long-tail needs are nobody's job; the gain is consistency and speed
en.TRUST_LABEL: Trust: no AI means no data sharing (docs)
en.STRUGGLE_LABEL: Learning curve: low; migration is the hard part
en.DELIGHT_1: Hands-on: typing the title Deep Work auto-filled the structured metadata — the closest the product comes to feeling intelligent, and it happens inside the free flow
en.DELIGHT_2: Hands-on: signup itself is the onboarding. No docs, no tutorial hunting
en.DELIGHT_3: The free tier gets unlimited objects, unlimited custom types, sync everywhere, import/export and view-only sharing (pricing page, all three tiers) — tidying is given away outright
en.STRUGGLE_1: Hands-on: bringing existing content in runs into type mismatch — the object types are its own, and your old notes have none of those fields
en.STRUGGLE_2: No AI on the free tier: the Basic row on the pricing table says AI not included. Anyone arriving because of the AI pitch hits the wall the first time they want to use it
en.STRUGGLE_3: Hands-on read, in the tester's own words: if you want to customise things, this is not the tool. Freedom has been traded away by design, not by omission
en.REVENUE_MODEL_NAME: Free core + Pro subscription + AI add-on (Plus)
en.REVENUE_MODEL_DETAIL: Pricing page (Hong Kong region, captured Nov 2026): Basic free forever; Pro HK$77.99/month and Believer HK$98.99/month at monthly billing, with 16% off annually; Plus, an add-on at HK$66.67/month billed annually, buys a much larger AI budget with top-ups available. The official comparison pages use a single USD figure: Pro at $9.99/month billed annually. Believer differs by supporting the team and early access to new features, not by more capability.
en.FREE_PAID_DETAIL: Free is structure plus storage: unlimited objects, spaces and custom types, sync everywhere, offline, import/export, view-only sharing, capture from WhatsApp / Telegram / email. Pro is retrieval plus review: AI assistant, smart queries, tasks, calendar integration, semantic search, version history, unlinked mentions, whiteboards, Readwise / Kindle import, public API, image and PDF analysis. (Source: the three-tier comparison on the pricing page.)
en.MON_ENTRY_HEADLINE: Give tidying away, charge for retrieval
en.MON_ENTRY_DETAIL: Unlike peers that meter storage or object counts, it makes capacity unlimited — the thing users complain about most. Both paid layers only feel necessary after use: AI (let it read for me) and queries/calendar/tasks (let it schedule for me). The upside is that free users never run out of room to work; the downside is a gap between the AI note-taking pitch and the free experience.
en.UX_MON_HEADLINE: Mostly aligned, with one structural tension
en.UX_MON_DETAIL_ARE_THEY_ALIGNED_OR_IN_TEN: Aligned: the free tier does not cripple the core promise (structure, sync, export), and the thicker the graph the more reason to upgrade. Two tensions: (1) AI is the loudest claim yet sits entirely behind the paywall, so the first attempt always hits it; (2) the company states it will not build end-to-end encryption, and using AI shares data with model providers (docs) — a paying individual has to accept both at once.
en.COMP_INTRO: The comparison below is my judgement, not a score or a measurement. The AI column rates first-party capability, not community plugins.
en.COMP_WHERE_OWN_WINS: Structure out of the box and time to first value. It is the only thing it dares put in a slogan: Stop building your system. Testing confirmed it — onboarding sits inside signup, the first note took a minute, and there was never a where-do-I-click moment.
en.COMP_WHERE_RIVALS_CATCH: Ownership and freedom. Anytype and Obsidian make “the files are yours” the default; Obsidian's ecosystem is what Capacities structurally gave up (its own comparison page cites 2,700+ community plugins, while the Obsidian community site counted 10,194 in Nov 2026 — comparison-page numbers age, which is itself a signal). Team collaboration went to Notion, and it does not intend to compete there.
en.CHANNEL_1: Six official comparison pages harvesting long-tail search (/compare/obsidian, evernote, notion, tana, heptabase, anytype all return 200)
en.CHANNEL_2: Reddit and Discord word of mouth (the site claims 10,000+ community members) — the why page quotes r/capacitiesapp users verbatim
en.CHANNEL_3: Three Product Hunt launches (30 May 2023, 12 Jul 2023, 25 Jul 2024) holding a 4.8 rating
en.GROWTH_LOOP_1_DETAIL: Comparison pages plus migration guides in the docs (Obsidian import guide, switching guide). It deliberately serves people arriving from elsewhere — the shortest path to payment, because they have already paid tuition once.
en.GROWTH_LOOP_2_DETAIL: A 10,000-person Discord and a subreddit; the artefact that spreads is “this is what my object page looks like”. With no plugin marketplace, the ecosystem travels as templates and screenshots rather than code.
en.HORIZONTAL_1: Clients everywhere: web, Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android (all listed in one line on the pricing page)
en.HORIZONTAL_2: AI Chat Connectors: ChatGPT / Claude / Cursor read and write your objects (Pro row on the pricing page)
en.VERTICAL_1: Personal knowledge management: researchers, writers, lifelong learners (the comparison pages' Best For)
en.VERTICAL_2: Teams and collaboration: explicitly out of scope (whats-not-next: Collaboration and Team plans are on hold)
en.PLATFORM_1: Public REST API 2.0 with a TypeScript SDK on Pro — third parties can read and write objects
en.PLATFORM_2: No plugin marketplace: whats-not-next rules plugins out, so extensibility goes through the API only
en.CURRENT_AI_USAGE_PARAGRAPH: All AI sits at Pro and above. Capability surface (docs): AI Chat inside Explore, a selection AI panel (translate / rewrite / summarise), auto-tagging, auto-collection, property auto-fill, image analysis including OCR and handwriting, /Ask AI, and AI-generated queries. The stated position is restrained: whats-next says AI should stay assistive, grounded in your notes and never in the way of your own thinking. Hands-on: the free tier genuinely has no AI, and the wall fires on AI and on tasks/Explore; without AI, data is not shared with model providers (docs), and that privacy notice was visible during testing.
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_1: Not shipped (my read): upgrade property auto-fill into proposing a whole object structure after reading messy material — today it fills existing fields, it does not propose structure
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_2: Not shipped (my read): let Connectors go from creating and editing a single object to restructuring a whole space in bulk (API 2.0 already provides the read foundation)
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_3: Not shipped (my read): a structure audit that flags objects missing the fields an AI needs. It is the one position that needs no model of its own, only its object model
en.AI_OPPORTUNITY_1: (my read) What it should build is not a stronger AI but a reusable asset: standard property sets for books, meetings, clients and projects. The hands-on reaction was that the structure itself is worth learning and feeding to one's own AI — users already treat it as a schema supplier; the company just has not productised it
en.AI_OPPORTUNITY_2: (my read) Turn API 2.0 and Connectors into an agent's memory backend: agents write logs, conclusions and to-dos into the object layer and the human confirms. That is the only path from note app to infrastructure
en.AI_DISRUPTION_RISK: (my read) The threat is not a rival adding AI but a general-purpose agent growing its own object model. Once ChatGPT or Claude maintains your personal knowledge graph, nobody pays a second subscription for the shape of an object page — the cleaning layer it does for agents today is exactly what agents will do themselves
en.METRICS_INTRO: The company discloses neither activity nor conversion. The three cards below combine verifiable numbers with explicitly marked inference — no fake precision.
en.NORTH_STAR_WHY: Basis: its value only exists when you open it and write a little each day (the daily note is the only daily-frequency entry point); the site publishes one big number, 50,000+ active knowledge workers, with no DAU/WAU definition
en.INPUT_METRIC_1_WHY: Basis: the company calls itself fully independent with a team of seven (whats-next), so Pro is the main beam; at $9.99/month, team size and subscriber count constrain each other
en.INPUT_METRIC_2_NAME: AI credits consumed and Plus attach rate [inferred]
en.INPUT_METRIC_2_WHY: Basis: Plus (HK$66.67/month annual) is its only second-order monetisation lever, and the pricing page documents top-ups and auto top-up — evidence it is being designed as a revenue line
en.INPUT_METRIC_3_WHY: Basis: the daily note is the core loop's entry point and the clearest divergence from Obsidian and Notion; its trend says more about adoption than total object count
en.GUARDRAIL_WHY: Basis: of 40 sampled App Store reviews most are 1-3 stars, landing on a sharesheet broken for months, syncing that needs an app restart and broken iPad layout — “Desktop is Lifechanging, iOS is Barely Functional” is a review title. If capture breaks, desktop excellence cannot outrun the rating
en.METRIC_BLINDSPOT_WHY: Hands-on read: the biggest weakness is type mismatch when importing existing content. Internally such failures are most likely logged as a successful import, because the objects were created — they are simply empty of fields
en.FRICTION_1_TITLE: Types do not match when you move in
en.FRICTION_1_BODY_WHY_IT_MATTERS: Hands-on: the object types are its own and your old notes carry none of those fields, so importing is not the same as using. It is the flip side of the out-of-the-box promise: a clean start for new users, no path for existing libraries.
en.FRICTION_2_BODY: A 3-star review is literally titled “Desktop is Lifechanging, iOS is Barely Functional”; the same batch reports a sharesheet broken for many months, syncing that requires restarting the app, and no object creation on iPad. Capture is the only thing mobile is for.
en.FRICTION_3_BODY: Hands-on, in the tester's words: if you want to customise things, it is not for you. No plugins, no formulas or advanced automation (whats-not-next lists both), so the ceiling for power users is low — this is not a tinkerer's tool.
en.FRICTION_4_TITLE: Zero AI on free contradicts the pitch
en.FRICTION_4_BODY: Verifiable on the pricing table: the Basic row says AI not included. Externally it is often filed as an AI note app, so the first attempt to use AI meets a paywall. Not a design flaw, but a positioning gap: the copy sells a studio, users hear AI.
en.RISK_INTRO: Only risks with public evidence are listed; severity and likelihood are my judgement, not quantified.
en.RISK_1_LIK: Of 40 App Store reviews most are 1-3 stars, clustered on the sharesheet, sync and iPad layout
en.RISK_1_MIT: Treat mobile as a capture-only component with a single hard target: under three seconds to record (my suggestion)
en.RISK_2_NAME: A structural gap in the privacy story
en.RISK_2_LIK: whats-not-next states no end-to-end encryption; using AI shares part of the data with model providers (docs)
en.RISK_2_MIT: Make “no AI, no sharing” a visible switch plus an annual transparency report (my suggestion)
en.RISK_3_NAME: General-purpose agents grow their own object layer
en.RISK_3_LIK: ChatGPT / Claude / Cursor can already create and edit its objects through Connectors (pricing page); the channel works in both directions
en.RISK_3_MIT: Race to be the de facto schema and write protocol — retreat from interface to substrate (my suggestion)
en.RISK_4_NAME: One subscription price and a seven-person team
en.RISK_4_LIK: Self-described team of seven, fully independent; a single Pro price tier caps the visible scale at 50,000 active users × $9.99
en.RISK_4_MIT: Make Plus a real second revenue line, or open API and non-team enterprise scenarios (my suggestion)
en.OPP_1_DETAIL_WHAT_HOW_WHY: (my read) Its public weakness is type mismatch after import. A one-off migration plus type mapping — translating old Notion or Obsidian structures into its object types — is cheap to build, certain in demand, and aimed at people who have already shown willingness to pay tuition.
en.OPP_2_HEADLINE: Field design as a reusable asset
en.OPP_2_DETAIL: (my read) Its object types are a ready-made schema: book, person, meeting, project. The hands-on reaction was immediate — this structure is worth learning and giving to an AI. The company treats it as an internal default and ships it undocumented; template packs and vertical editions (investment research, consulting, clinicians) are a revenue line that needs no new engineering.
en.OPP_3_DETAIL: (my read) Users do not know which objects an AI cannot read. A checklist of missing fields, missing links and missing context would move it from pretty notes to an agent-readable knowledge base — and it depends on the object model, not on model capability.
en.STRATEGIC_HEADLINE: From note app to the structured memory layer for agents
en.STRATEGIC_DETAIL_HIGH_IMPACT_BET: (my read) Its real differentiation is not AI but the cleaning it has already done: people, books, meetings and projects abstracted into typed objects with fields. The bet should be making that structure the default schema agents read and write (API 2.0 and Connectors are already there), not chasing model capability feature by feature.
en.MOONSHOT_HEADLINE: Make its object spec the default structure of personal AI
en.MOONSHOT_DETAIL_WHY_IT_COULD_RESHAPE_THE: (my read) If agents write contacts, books and projects using its fields, Capacities stops being an app and becomes the schema layer of personal AI — the analogy is not Notion but a database driver. A team of seven cannot build models, but it can build a standard; once adopted, the migration arrow points the other way.
en.FINAL_WINS: Structure out of the box and the object model: nothing to build, types on day one, first note in a minute
en.FINAL_BREAKS: Mobile (capture is broken) and migration (types do not match), plus the customisation ceiling
en.FINAL_MOAT_OR_LACK_THEREOF: The moat is the feeling that nobody wants someone else's system — not the technology. The object model is copyable; convincing users that this time they will not have to build anything is not. The same logic means it cannot stop general-purpose agents from eating the object layer from above.

extra_zh.title: 对标竞品地图
extra_zh.body:
先给一个探测结果，因为它是结论的一部分。2026-11-11 逐个打开路径：/compare、/compare/obsidian、/compare/evernote、/compare/notion、/compare/tana、/compare/heptabase、/compare/anytype 全部 200；而 /vs、/alternatives、/switch 全部 404。

也就是说，它把「打谁」写进了 URL 结构里：六个竞品是它自己点名要打的，其余打法（against / vs / switch 这类常见换用词）它一个都没建。这件事本身就是判断依据——它只做「存量迁移者的比较」，不做「泛替代品」。我的判断：对比页的读者不是正在选工具的人，而是已经有一库笔记、正在找理由搬家的人。

谁抢的是哪一段它更近的地方
Notion团队知识库与协作多人、权限、企业采购（它明确不抢）
Obsidian本地文件与自由度数据所有权、插件生态（它明确不做）
Evernote上一代的收集习惯存量用户与剪藏，迁移意愿最高
Tanasupertag 的工作流型笔记重流程用户的查询能力
Heptabase白板式学习与研究可视化思考，适合研究者
Anytype本地加密的对象空间隐私叙事与 P2P

PH 的 Similar Products 给的是另一套名单（Obsidian、Craft.do、Bear、Reflect、Tana）——用户视角的相似不等于官方视角的对手：官方挑的是「能被打成配置负担重」的对手，用户挑的是「看起来一样轻」的工具。

extra_zh.title: 竞品技术底座
extra_zh.body:
四个对比维度看底座，一句话一家：

产品底座选择锁住了什么锁死了什么
Capacities云端对象存储 + 全内建功能 + 无插件开箱一致性与速度隐私叙事、长尾扩展（无 E2EE、无插件）
Obsidian本地 Markdown 文件 + 社区插件可迁移、可被 agent 直接读写开箱即用（一切要自己搭）
Notion云端块 + 数据库团队协作与权限个人场景的配置成本
Tanasupertag 大纲 + 查询重流程工作流学习曲线最陡
Anytype本地优先 + P2P + E2E + 开源隐私与所有权同步稳定性与生态速度

我的判断：Capacities 的底座选择是「用不做换一致性」。它放弃了三个可扩展性入口（插件、E2EE、协作），换来的是「打开就知道干什么」。这不是能力不足，是刻意的取舍——whats-not-next 把这三件事都写成了公开立场。

extra_zh.title: 可迁移的机会
extra_zh.body:
三条我认为可以直接拿走的做法，都不需要重写代码：

1. 官方对比页 + 官方「不做什么」页，是零成本的信任与 GEO 资产。它两件事都做了：六个 /compare 页吃长尾搜索，/whats-not-next 把「我们不做什么」写成公开清单。后者尤其少见——它把路线外的东西变成承诺，同时替用户做完了筛选。任何 to-C 工具都能抄这一套。

2. 它的公开短板就是生意：迁移时的类型映射。实测（燃冰）的最大感受是「搬进来类型对不上」。做一次性迁移服务（Notion / Obsidian → 它的对象类型），吃到的是意愿最强的一批用户。

3. 它的字段设计本身就是资产。书、人、会议、项目这四类对象的属性集，是现成的 schema。实测时的直接反应是「这套结构值得学，喂给自己的 AI」。官方把它当内部默认值，对外零文档化——这是一个没被产品化的机会。

extra_zh.title: 流量与变现拆解
extra_zh.body:
钱从哪来：从「买了三四个笔记软件、还没找到系统」的知识工作者兜里出。这批人付费意愿已被验证（他们为上一款工具付过费），痛点是配置疲劳，不是功能缺失。

凭什么拿到：对比页吃意图最靠近付费的长尾搜索（capacities vs obsidian / evernote / notion）＋ Reddit / Discord 的口碑（官网自述 1 万+ 社区成员）＋ PH 三次发布长期挂 4.8 分。它没有投广告的证据，全部是搜索与口碑。

变现三层：Basic（免费）→ Pro / Believer（订阅，官网对比页口径 $9.99/月 年付）→ Plus（AI 额度加购，HK$66.67/月 年付，可再买 top-up）。最脆的一根梁是「AI 在付费墙后」：它对外被当成 AI 笔记，免费版却零 AI，第一次想用 AI 就是转化点——这是转化率最高、也最容易流失的一刻。

我的判断：这套结构里真正聪明的是「整理白送、调用收钱」。容量和对象数量做到无限，把抱怨最多的维度从免费档拿掉；收钱的两层都只在「用起来之后」才有感觉。缺点是无法靠免费版建立「它很智能」的预期。

extra_zh.title: 官方「不做」清单与替代路径
extra_zh.body:
/whats-not-next（2026-11 可访问）把不做的事写成了公开清单，原文归类如下：平板手写、公式与高级自动化、闪卡与间隔重复、RTL 语言、协作与团队版（on hold）、对象继承、端到端加密、终身订阅、插件。这份清单的价值在于：它不是「暂缺」，是「路线外」，用户不必等。

替代路径（离开它怎么走）：导出侧三个档位都支持 Markdown / CSV（定价页原文 Import and export to Markdown, CSV, and more，全档含），所以搬走不靠它批准；API 2.0 与 TypeScript SDK（Pro）让对象可以批量取出。想回去 Obsidian 的人拿得到 md，想去 Notion 的人拿得到表格。

我的判断：不做 E2EE 与不做插件，是同一个取舍的两面——它们都会拖慢一致性与速度。这个取舍在「个人 + 云端 + AI」的组合里是合理的；但它同时意味着，凡把隐私当第一需求的用户，注定流向 Anytype 或 Obsidian，这不是产品体验能挽回的部分。

extra_en.title: Competitive map
extra_en.body:
Start with a probe result, because the probe is part of the conclusion. Paths opened one by one on 11 Nov 2026: /compare, /compare/obsidian, /compare/evernote, /compare/notion, /compare/tana, /compare/heptabase and /compare/anytype all return 200; /vs, /alternatives and /switch all return 404.

In other words, it writes its targets into the URL structure: six named rivals, and none of the usual alternative framings. That is itself evidence — it only builds comparison pages for people migrating off something, never for people shopping around. My read: the reader of those pages is not choosing a tool, they already own a library and are looking for a reason to move.

WhoWhich slice they takeWhere they sit closer
NotionTeam wikis and collaborationMultiplayer, permissions, enterprise procurement (explicitly not contested)
ObsidianLocal files and freedomOwnership, plugin ecosystem (explicitly not built)
EvernoteLast-generation collecting habitsInstalled base, highest migration intent
TanaSupertag workflow notesQuery power for process-heavy users
HeptabaseWhiteboard learning and researchVisual thinking, researcher fit
AnytypeLocally encrypted object spacesPrivacy narrative and P2P

Product Hunt's Similar Products offers a different list (Obsidian, Craft.do, Bear, Reflect, Tana) — similarity from the user's side is not rivalry from the company's side. The company picks rivals it can frame as configuration burden; users pick tools that look equally light.

extra_en.title: Competitor technical stack
extra_en.body:
Four dimensions, one line each:

ProductStack choiceWhat it locks inWhat it locks out
CapacitiesCloud object store + everything first-party + no pluginsOut-of-the-box consistency and speedPrivacy narrative and long-tail extension (no E2EE, no plugins)
ObsidianLocal Markdown files + community pluginsPortability, direct agent read/writeUsability on day one (you build everything)
NotionCloud blocks + databasesTeam collaboration and permissionsConfiguration cost for solo users
TanaSupertag outlines + queriesProcess-heavy workflowsThe steepest learning curve
AnytypeLocal-first + P2P + E2E + open sourcePrivacy and ownershipSync reliability and ecosystem speed

My read: Capacities chose consistency by refusing things. It gives up three extensibility doors (plugins, E2EE, collaboration) in exchange for opening the app and knowing what to do. This is a deliberate trade, not a capability gap — whats-not-next publishes all three as positions.

extra_en.title: Transferable opportunities
extra_en.body:
Three practices worth taking, none of which requires rewriting code:

1. Official comparison pages plus an official will-not-build page are free trust and GEO assets. It does both: six /compare pages harvest long-tail search, and /whats-not-next publishes what it will never ship. The latter is rare — it turns out-of-scope items into promises and does the user's screening for them. Any consumer tool can copy this.

2. Its public weakness is a business: type mapping on migration. The strongest hands-on impression was that importing runs into type mismatch. A one-off migration service (Notion / Obsidian structures into its object types) serves the highest-intent users available.

3. Its field design is an asset in itself. The property sets for books, people, meetings and projects are a ready-made schema. The hands-on reaction was that the structure is worth learning and feeding to one's own AI. The company treats it as an internal default and documents it nowhere — an unproductised opportunity.

extra_en.title: Traffic and monetisation
extra_en.body:
Where the money comes from: knowledge workers on their third or fourth note app who still have not found a system. Their willingness to pay is already proven — they paid for the previous tool. The pain is configuration fatigue, not missing features.

How it reaches them: comparison pages harvesting the search intents closest to purchase (capacities vs obsidian / evernote / notion), Reddit and Discord word of mouth (the site claims 10,000+ community members), and three Product Hunt launches holding 4.8. There is no evidence of paid advertising — this is search and reputation.

Three monetisation layers: Basic (free) → Pro / Believer (subscription, $9.99/month billed annually per the comparison pages) → Plus (AI credit add-on at HK$66.67/month billed annually, with top-ups). The most fragile beam is AI behind the paywall: the market files it as an AI note app, the free tier has none, so the first attempt at AI is both the highest-conversion and highest-churn moment.

My read: the clever part is giving tidying away and charging for retrieval. Capacity and object counts are unlimited, removing the most-complained-about dimension from the free tier, while both paid layers only feel necessary after use. The cost is that the free tier cannot establish the expectation that it is intelligent.

extra_en.title: The official will-not-build list and the exit path
extra_en.body:
/whats-not-next (live Nov 2026) publishes the refusals: tablet handwriting, formulas and advanced automation, flashcards and spaced repetition, RTL languages, collaboration and team plans (on hold), object inheritance, end-to-end encryption, lifetime subscriptions and plugins. The value of the list is that these are out of scope rather than pending — users need not wait.

The exit path: export supports Markdown and CSV on all three tiers (pricing page: Import and export to Markdown, CSV, and more — included on all), so leaving does not require permission; API 2.0 and the TypeScript SDK on Pro let objects be pulled out in bulk. Anyone returning to Obsidian gets Markdown; anyone moving to Notion gets tables.

My read: refusing E2EE and refusing plugins are two sides of one trade — both would slow down consistency and speed. That trade is sensible for personal, cloud, AI-assisted use; but it also means anyone who puts privacy first is destined for Anytype or Obsidian, and no amount of interface polish wins them back.
